en: to smart; to throb; to tingle

examples.ko: 어제 운동을 너무 많이 해서 다리가 욱신거려요.
examples.en: I exercised too much yesterday, so my legs are throbbing.

examples.ko: 이가 계속 욱신거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My tooth kept throbbing, so I couldn't sleep.
Does the knee you fell on still throb?

examples.ko: 비가 오려고 하면 어깨가 욱신거리기 시작해요.
examples.en: When it's about to rain, my shoulder starts to ache.

examples.ko: 손가락이 욱신거리는데 병원에 가 봐야 할까요?
examples.en: My finger is throbbing. Should I go to the hospital?

examples.ko: 약을 먹었더니 욱신거리던 머리가 좀 나아졌어요.
examples.en: After I took medicine, my throbbing head got a bit better.

explain: 그냥 '아프다'보다 맥박 치듯 계속 쑤시는 느낌이에요. 다치거나 부딪친 곳, 근육통, 치통에 자주 써요. 보통 '다리가 욱신거려요'처럼 아픈 부위를 주어로 말해요.

phrases.en: My knee that I fell on throbs with pain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '욱신거리다'의 부사형으로 계속 쑤시는 통증을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form stresses a continuous throbbing pain.

phrases.en: My shoulder throbbed, so I went to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통증 때문에 어떤 일이 생겼다고 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to give pain as the reason for something.

phrases.en: The throbbing pain continued all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 통증의 종류를 설명할 때 명사 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before 'pain' to describe its kind.

explain_en: It is more specific than plain '아프다': a dull pain that keeps pulsing. It is often used for injuries, muscle soreness and toothaches. You usually make the sore body part the subject, as in '다리가 욱신거려요'.

en: to palpitate; to throb; to thump

examples.ko: 발표 전에 가슴이 울렁여서 물을 마셨어요.
examples.en: My heart was fluttering before the presentation, so I drank some water.
As soon as I got on the boat, my stomach started to heave.
My heart flutters when I see the person I like.
I could feel the boat rolling on the waves.

examples.ko: 차 안에서 책을 읽었더니 속이 울렁였어요.
examples.en: I read a book in the car, and my stomach felt queasy.

examples.ko: 합격 소식에 가슴이 울렁이던 순간이 아직 기억나요.
examples.en: I still remember the moment my heart fluttered at the news that I passed.

explain: 가슴에 쓰면 설렘이나 긴장으로 두근거리는 느낌이고, 속에 쓰면 멀미처럼 메스꺼운 느낌이에요. 어느 쪽인지는 '가슴이', '속이' 같은 앞말로 알 수 있어요. '울렁거리다'도 비슷하게 쓰여요.

phrases.en: My stomach feels queasy when I ride a bus for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '울렁이다'와 거의 같고, 멀미나 메스꺼움을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as '울렁이다'; often used for motion sickness or nausea.

phrases.example: 울렁이는 가슴을 진정시키려고 숨을 크게 쉬었어요.
phrases.en: I took a deep breath to calm my pounding heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 설렘이나 긴장으로 두근거리는 가슴을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a heart pounding from excitement or nervousness.

phrases.en: My heart fluttered when I heard I had passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거 해요체로, 지나간 순간의 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite past form for a feeling in a past moment.

explain_en: With '가슴' it means a fluttering heart from excitement or nerves, and with '속' it means a queasy, motion-sickness feeling. The word before it, '가슴이' or '속이', tells you which. '울렁거리다' is used in a similar way.

examples.ko: 밀폐된 공간에서 숯불을 피우면 질식할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you burn charcoal in an enclosed space, you can suffocate.

examples.ko: 연기 때문에 질식할 것 같아서 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: I felt like I was suffocating from the smoke, so I opened the window.

examples.ko: 사우나 안이 너무 답답해서 질식하는 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: It was so stuffy in the sauna that I thought I would suffocate.

examples.ko: 사고 현장에서 한 사람이 질식해서 병원으로 옮겨졌어요.
examples.en: One person suffocated at the accident site and was taken to the hospital.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 수증기 때문에 질식해 버릴 것 같았어요.
examples.en: It felt like I would suffocate from the hot steam.

examples.ko: 질식하지 않게 환기를 자주 해 주세요.
examples.en: Please ventilate often so that no one suffocates.

explain: '숨이 막히다'와 달리 산소가 부족하거나 공기가 막혀서 정말 숨을 쉬기 어려운 상황에 써요. 뉴스에서는 '질식 위험', '질식사'처럼 자주 나와요. 답답한 분위기를 말할 때 '질식할 것 같다'도 쓰지만, 일상 대화에서는 '숨 막히다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The smoke was so heavy that I almost suffocated.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 뻔하다'는 거의 그럴 뻔했지만 아니었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: -ㄹ 뻔하다 means it almost happened but didn't.

phrases.en: In fires, many people die from suffocation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨을 못 쉬어서 죽는 경우를 가리키는 뉴스 용어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news term for death caused by not being able to breathe.

phrases.en: A sealed room carries a risk of suffocation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전 안내에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation common in safety notices.

explain_en: Unlike '숨이 막히다', it is used when you really cannot breathe because of lack of oxygen or blocked air. In the news you often see '질식 위험' and '질식사'. '질식할 것 같다' can describe a stifling mood too, but in daily talk '숨 막히다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: My grandfather's hearing has become much weaker.
They tested my hearing at the health checkup.

examples.ko: 큰 소리를 오래 들으면 청력에 해로워요.
examples.en: Listening to loud sounds for a long time is harmful to your hearing.
Cats have better hearing than people.
My hearing got worse, so I bought a hearing aid.
A hearing test doesn't hurt.

explain: '청력이 좋다/나쁘다/약하다'처럼 능력을 말할 때 써요. 같은 종류의 '시력(눈)'이 있어요. 소리를 잘 듣는지 말할 때는 '귀가 밝다/어둡다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Children have good hearing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 잘 듣는 능력을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a good ability to hear.

phrases.en: I had a hearing test at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 건강검진에서 자주 듣는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase at hospitals and checkups.

phrases.en: Hearing gets worse as you get older.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣는 힘이 약해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the ability to hear gets weaker.

explain_en: It is used for the ability itself: 청력이 좋다, 나쁘다, 약하다. Its partner for the eyes is 시력. Informally, people also say 귀가 밝다 or 귀가 어둡다 about someone's hearing.

en: to be plump; to be chubby

examples.en: The baby's arms are plump.
Lots of plump chestnuts grew on the tree.
The puppy's cheeks are chubby, so it's cute.
These are chicks that have grown plump.
My nephew's hands are chubby and warm.
The sweet potatoes are plump, so they'll probably be tasty.

explain: 살이 보기 좋게 올라 통통하다는 뜻이고, 귀엽고 건강한 느낌이라 아기나 동물, 알이 찬 열매에 써요. '살찌다'는 단순히 체중이 늘 때 쓰고, '토실토실하다'는 칭찬하는 말투예요. 사람의 몸을 두고 어른에게 말하면 조심해야 해요.

phrases.en: The chubby baby smiles brightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때는 '토실토실한'으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 토실토실한 before a noun.

phrases.en: The puppy has plumped up nicely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강하게 살이 붙었을 때 좋은 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in a positive sense for healthy weight gain.

phrases.en: The baby's cheeks are chubby and cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉬운 비슷한 말이에요. 둘 다 귀여운 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier, similar word. Both have a cute feeling.

explain_en: It describes a pleasantly filled-out look, with a cute and healthy feel, so it is used for babies, animals, and full ripe fruit. '살찌다' simply means gaining weight, while '토실토실하다' is a warm, complimentary tone. Be careful about saying it about an adult's body.

en: to suck; to inhale; to breathe in

examples.en: I wear a mask so I don't inhale dust.
This vacuum cleaner sucks up even tiny bits of trash.

examples.ko: 의사가 약을 흡입하는 방법을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The doctor showed me how to inhale the medicine.
I inhaled a lot of smoke and now I'm coughing.

examples.ko: 기계가 공기를 흡입한 다음 필터로 걸러요.
examples.en: The machine takes in air and then filters it.

examples.ko: 약을 깊게 흡입했다가 천천히 숨을 내쉬세요.
examples.en: Inhale the medicine deeply, then breathe out slowly.

explain: '들이마시다'보다 딱딱한 말로, 의사의 설명이나 안전 안내, 기계 설명서에 자주 나와요. 사람이 숨을 쉬는 것뿐 아니라 청소기나 기계가 공기나 먼지를 빨아들일 때도 써요.

phrases.en: This vacuum cleaner has good suction power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청소기 같은 기계가 빨아들이는 힘을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The sucking power of machines like vacuum cleaners.

phrases.en: Try taking a deep breath in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '흡입하다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 숨을 쉴 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 흡입하다 and common for breathing in daily life.

phrases.en: This machine sucks in water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 액체나 먼지를 안으로 당길 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy word for pulling liquid or dust inside.

explain_en: To inhale — formal, breathing in dust, gas or smoke (흡입하다) It is a stiffer word than 들이마시다 and shows up in doctors' explanations, safety notices, and machine manuals. It covers both people breathing something in and machines like vacuum cleaners drawing in air or dust.

t90.ax: I wear a mask so I don't inhale dust.

examples.en: On busy days I eat convenience food for dinner.
The convenience store's ready meals have become really varied.
You just heat the convenience food in the microwave.
I live alone, so I often buy ready meals.
The ready-meal market is growing every year.

examples.ko: 이 간편식은 맛도 괜찮고 값도 싸요.
examples.en: This ready meal tastes decent and is cheap too.

explain: 도시락, 즉석밥, 냉동식품처럼 빠르고 쉽게 먹을 수 있게 만든 음식이에요. 뉴스에서는 '간편식 시장'처럼 소비 이야기에서 많이 나와요. 일상에서는 '즉석식품', '편의점 도시락'처럼 구체적으로 말해요.

phrases.en: When I'm busy, I often eat instant food.
phrases.nuance_ko: '간편식'과 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서 더 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 간편식 but more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: I ate a convenience store lunch box for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간편식 중에서 구체적인 음식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Names a specific kind of convenience food.

phrases.en: The convenience food market keeps growing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 소비 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in news stories about spending and sales.

explain_en: It covers foods made to be eaten quickly and easily, such as lunch boxes, instant rice and frozen food. In the news it appears in consumer talk such as '간편식 시장'. In daily speech people are more specific, saying '즉석식품' or '편의점 도시락'.

examples.en: When kimchi-making season comes, the price of napa cabbage goes up.
My family gathers every kimchi-making season.
The market is really crowded during kimchi-making season.

examples.ko: 김장철을 맞아 마트에서 소금 할인을 해요.
examples.en: For kimchi-making season, the supermarket is discounting salt.
I ordered chili powder to get ready for kimchi-making season.
This year even during kimchi-making season, the weather is warm.

explain: 겨울을 대비해 김치를 많이 담그는 늦가을 무렵을 말해요. '철'은 '휴가철', '장마철'처럼 어떤 일이 많은 시기를 뜻하고, 짝말로 '김장하다', '김장 김치'가 있어요.

phrases.en: This year we make kimchi at my aunt's house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨울에 먹을 김치를 담근다는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for making kimchi for winter.

phrases.en: We eat the winter kimchi all through the winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그때 담근 김치를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the kimchi made at that time.

phrases.en: During kimchi season the market is very crowded.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-에는'을 붙여 그 시기의 특징을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -에는 describes what that season is like.

explain_en: It refers to the late-autumn period when people make a lot of kimchi to prepare for winter. '철' means a season when something is common, as in '휴가철' and '장마철', and related words are '김장하다' and '김장 김치'.

examples.en: You must cook raw meat before eating it.
I wonder if it's okay to give raw meat to a cat.
Wash your hands right away after touching raw meat.
I use separate cutting boards for raw meat and vegetables.
The fridge smells like raw meat.
I ate raw meat by mistake and got a stomachache.

explain: '날-'은 익히지 않은 것에 붙어요. 날달걀, 날것처럼 짝으로 같이 알아 두세요. 불에 익힌 고기는 '익힌 고기'라고 하고, 날고기는 '생고기'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Please keep raw meat in the fridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고 요리나 식당 얘기에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, common in cooking and restaurant talk.

phrases.example: 날고기를 먹으면 배탈이 날 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Eating raw meat can upset your stomach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 익히지 않고 먹는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Talks about eating meat without cooking it.

phrases.en: Please cook raw meat well before eating.
phrases.nuance_ko: '익히다'와 함께 요리하는 방법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 익히다 it talks about how to cook it.

explain_en: '날-' attaches to things that are not cooked, as in 날달걀 and 날것. Cooked meat is '익힌 고기', and raw meat is also called '생고기'.

en: gamey smell; rank smell of meat

examples.ko: 고기를 구울 때 누린내가 나서 환기를 했어요.
examples.en: The meat gave off a gamey smell when grilling, so I aired out the room.

examples.ko: 양고기는 누린내 때문에 못 먹는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people can't eat lamb because of its gamey smell.

examples.ko: 생강을 넣으면 고기 누린내를 없앨 수 있어요.
examples.en: Adding ginger can get rid of the gamey smell of meat.

examples.ko: 이 집 곰탕은 누린내도 안 나고 국물이 깔끔해요.
examples.en: This place's beef bone soup has no gamey smell and the broth is clean.

examples.ko: 누린내 제거에는 우유에 담그는 방법도 있어요.
examples.en: Soaking in milk is another way to remove the gamey smell.

examples.ko: 염소 고기 특유의 누린내가 익숙하지 않아요.
examples.en: I'm not used to the gamey smell typical of goat meat.

explain: '비린내'는 생선 냄새이고 '누린내'는 고기나 털에서 나는 냄새예요. 요리할 때는 '잡내'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: This meat has a gamey smell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고기에서 냄새가 날 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for when meat smells gamey.

phrases.example: 생강을 넣으면 누린내를 없앨 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Adding ginger can get rid of the gamey smell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 냄새를 줄이는 방법을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about how to reduce the smell in cooking.

phrases.example: 우유에 담가 두면 고기 잡내가 줄어요.
phrases.en: Soaking meat in milk reduces its off smell.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 누린내와 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cooking term used much like 누린내.

explain_en: '비린내' is the smell of fish, while '누린내' is the smell that comes from meat or animal hair. When cooking, people also say '잡내'.

examples.en: I bought deodeok at the market and grilled it to eat.

examples.ko: 더덕은 향이 진해서 좋아하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Deodeok has a strong aroma, and many people like it.

examples.ko: 어머니가 더덕구이를 해 주셔서 밥을 두 그릇 먹었어요.
examples.en: My mother made grilled deodeok, so I ate two bowls of rice.

examples.ko: 더덕 껍질을 벗기는 게 은근히 힘들어요.
examples.en: Peeling deodeok is surprisingly hard.

examples.ko: 산에서 캔 더덕이라 향이 훨씬 좋아요.
examples.en: It's deodeok dug up in the mountains, so the aroma is much better.

examples.ko: 고추장 양념을 바른 더덕이 밥반찬으로 딱이에요.
examples.en: Deodeok with a red pepper paste marinade is perfect as a side dish for rice.

explain: 껍질을 벗겨 두드려서 구이나 무침으로 많이 먹어요. 쓴맛과 진한 향이 있어서 '더덕구이'처럼 양념을 해서 먹는 경우가 많아요. 비슷한 뿌리채소 '도라지'와 함께 한식에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I had grilled deodeok for dinner and the aroma was great.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양념을 발라 구운 요리 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the dish made by grilling it with seasoning.

phrases.en: My mother made seasoned deodeok for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양념에 무쳐 먹는 반찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A side dish where it is mixed with seasoning.

phrases.example: 더덕 껍질을 벗기면 향이 확 나요.
phrases.en: When you peel deodeok, the scent hits you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리하기 전에 준비하는 과정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the preparation step before cooking.

explain_en: People usually peel it, pound it, and eat it grilled or as a seasoned side dish. It has a slightly bitter taste and a strong aroma, so it is often cooked with seasoning, as in '더덕구이'. It often appears in Korean food together with another root vegetable, '도라지'.

en: to become desiccated; to be dried up

examples.en: I was away for a few days, and the plant pot dried up completely.
If you leave bread out, it dries up and gets hard.
I found a shriveled, dried-up tangerine in the fridge.

examples.ko: 김치 위쪽이 말라비틀어지기 전에 빨리 드세요.
examples.en: Please eat the kimchi quickly before the top dries out.
In the drought, all the grass ended up withered and dry.

examples.ko: 화분 속 잎이 말라비틀어져서 결국 버렸어요.
examples.en: The leaves in the pot dried up and shriveled, so I finally threw it away.

explain: 그냥 '마르다'보다 심해서 오그라들고 볼품없어진 느낌이 있어요. 식물, 빵, 과일처럼 물기가 빠진 것에 많이 쓰고, 사람에게 쓰면 매우 거친 말이 돼요. 활용은 '말라비틀어져요, 말라비틀어진'이에요.

phrases.en: A dried-up, shriveled piece of bread turned up in the corner of the fridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔서 물기가 빠져 볼품없어진 물건을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form, used to describe something that has lost its moisture and looks shriveled.

phrases.example: 물을 안 줬더니 꽃이 말라비틀어져 있어요.
phrases.en: I didn't water it, so the flowers are all dried up and shriveled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 그런 상태가 된 것을 보고 말할 때 '-아/어 있다'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-아/어 있다', it describes something that is already in that dried-up state.
phrases.en_equiv: to be dried up and shriveled

phrases.en: The sun was strong, so the laundry dried completely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물기가 완전히 없어질 때 쓰는 말로, 볼품없어진 느낌은 없어서 '말라비틀어지다'보다 덜 거칠어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means completely dry without the shriveled, ugly feel, so it is milder than '말라비틀어지다'.

explain_en: It is stronger than plain '마르다' and suggests something that has shriveled up and looks poor. It is common for plants, bread and fruit that lost their moisture, and sounds very harsh if used about people. It conjugates as '말라비틀어져요' and '말라비틀어진'.

examples.en: The baby is crying for food, probably because he's hungry.
Time for your food, sweetie.

examples.ko: 맘마 다 먹고 나면 같이 놀아요.
examples.en: When you finish your food, let's play together.
The child said 'mamma,' the baby word for food, for the first time.
My little nephew smiles whenever he sees his food.
Let's wash your hands before you eat.

explain: 어린아이에게 '밥'을 가리킬 때 쓰는 아기 말이에요. 어른끼리 이야기할 때는 쓰지 않고, 아이에게 말하거나 아이 이야기를 할 때 귀엽게 써요. '까까'(과자)도 같은 종류의 아기 말이에요.

phrases.en: The mother holds the baby saying, "Let's eat."
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기에게 반말로 부드럽게 권하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft, informal invitation said to a baby.

phrases.example: 엄마가 "우리 아가, 맘마 줄까요?" 하고 물어요.
phrases.en: The mother asks, "Shall I give you some food, little one?"
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기에게 존댓말로 다정하게 묻는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle question to a baby, offering food.
phrases.en_equiv: shall I give you food? (baby talk)

phrases.en: The dad smiles and asks, "Did you eat a lot?"
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기가 밥을 먹은 뒤에 반말로 묻는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An informal question asked to a baby after a meal.
phrases.en_equiv: did you eat a lot? (baby talk)

explain_en: Baby talk, said to or around very young children. It is baby talk for '밥' (food or a meal) used with small children. Adults don't use it with each other; you use it when talking to a child or cutely about a child. '까까' (snacks) is another word of the same kind.

en: to be squashy; to be mushy

examples.en: The persimmon is so ripe that it's mushy.
The banana is mushy, so I don't want to eat it.

examples.ko: 발밑에서 물컹한 느낌이 나서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I felt something squishy under my foot and was startled.
If you overcook eggplant, the texture turns mushy.
Please cook it just lightly so it doesn't get mushy.
The tofu I froze and thawed was mushy.

explain: 푹 익은 과일이나 삶은 채소처럼 눌러 보면 속이 무르게 들어가는 느낌이에요. 부드러운 것과 달리 식감이 별로라는 말투로 쓸 때가 많아요. '말랑하다'는 귀엽고 부드러운 느낌이라 쓰임이 조금 달라요.

phrases.en: I make juice out of mushy peaches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이고 너무 익은 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form; suggests the fruit is overripe.

phrases.en: The strawberries went mushy after being frozen and thawed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 단단하던 것이 변했다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the idea that something firm has changed.

phrases.en: This avocado isn't mushy, so it's good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식감이 좋다는 말을 부정형으로 표현할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form used to say the texture is fine.

explain_en: It describes the feeling of overripe fruit or boiled vegetables, where the inside gives way when pressed. Unlike simply 'soft', it is often said with a sense that the texture is unpleasant. '말랑하다' feels cute and soft, so its use is a bit different.
